name: Inverted firing
summary: A bowl is fired upside down on its rim in a ring of fireclay, so that the wall stays thin and true. The rim has no glaze and takes a metal band.
how: Throw a thin bowl and coat it with glaze.
Wipe the glaze from the rim.
Set the bowl rim-down on a stepped ring of fireclay.
Fire the stack, then bind the bare rim with copper or silver.

origin.note: Potters at the Ding kilns start to fire bowls upside down on their rims.

adoptions.via: Ding potters stack thin bowls rim-down in stepped saggar rings and bind the bare rims with metal.
